gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-hk: Technical from the first glance, Nippo has small letters standing almost capital-tall, every stroke looking cut from wire. Noto Sans HK follows with large lowercase forms and lifted ends, so paragraphs run along smoothly.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-imperial-arama: Wire-cut, nearly capital-sized lowercase in Nippo, with crossbars as fat as the stems. Noto Sans Imperial Aramaic then eases in with a c whose ends point apart, giving the heading's sturdy lines a friendlier partner.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-inscriptional-: Nippo's strokes look cut from wire, with stems and crossbars sharing one thickness and small letters standing nearly capital-sized. Noto Sans Inscriptional Parthian runs open-eyed and deep-bodied across a paragraph.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-jp: Nippo is a display face with strokes that look cut from wire. Its horizontals match its upright stems for punch, while Noto Sans JP brings a very tall x-height, plus curves that sweep open.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-kayah-li: Noto Sans Kayah Li reads smoothly, with brush ends lifted before curves close and capitals only slightly taller than lowercase. Nippo's wire-cut lines, all traced at one thickness, give this pair its edge.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-khmer: Noto Sans Khmer has generous openings like chisel notches in wood, with small letters standing nearly capital-sized. Nippo grabs the eye with flat fineliner lines; the body carries the text.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-khojki: Marker-plain and wire-cut, Nippo stands its small letters nearly capital-tall. Noto Sans Khojki lets light through its wide exits and large e eyes, and that openness is the pair's real draw.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-lao-looped: Noto Sans Lao Looped makes words read as solid blocks, its bowls left unfinished on one side. Nippo, meanwhile, grabs attention with horizontals matching its verticals in thickness, all cut like wire.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-lepcha: Approachable curves keep a wide opening in Noto Sans Lepcha, whose lowercase stands tall like cast iron capitals. Nippo adds punch up top, its pressure-free ballpoint line looking cut from wire.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-lydian: Nippo is all wire-cut lines traced with a single marker tip. Noto Sans Lydian follows with capitals barely taller than lowercase and an opening wide as a sprung paper clip.
